clue.text: Committed in a moment of abstraction ?

definitions.text: Committed in a moment of abstraction ?

parts.words: Committed in a moment of abstraction ?
parts.note: abstraction reads as absent-mindedness, but it also means taking something away, so the crime done is stealing

explanation.walkthrough: A 'moment of abstraction' looks like day-dreaming; here abstraction is its other sense, the removing of property.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstracting goods is a formal term for stealing, which is the crime committed.

clue.text: For which bell-ringers use the telephone ?

definitions.text: For which bell-ringers use the telephone ?

parts.words: For which bell-ringers use the telephone ?
parts.note: bell-ringers toll bells, and a long-distance telephone call that is charged extra bears the same name

explanation.walkthrough: Ringers toll; a trunk call charged at a higher rate is a toll call.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged long-distance telephone connections are named for the toll, or fee, paid.

clue.text: The fairies follow ours for us

indicators.note: follow means the fairies come after ours, so taking ours away from the start of the longer word leaves them

parts.note: ourselves is an emphatic form of us

explanation.walkthrough: Put these fairies after OURS and you get OURSELVES, which stands for 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small magical beings, a kind of fairy folk.

clue.text: Support for, one in a culinary, hole?

definitions.text: Support for, one in a culinary, hole?

parts.words: Support for, one in a culinary, hole?
parts.note: toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages in batter, and a seat or support for a toad is a fungus in folklore

explanation.walkthrough: Toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages baked in batter; the toad's seat, its stool, is the fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk name for a mushroom-shaped fungus is a seat on which a toad sits.

clue.text: There's no sense in a dirty bus, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a random, careless fashion, so the letters of the phrase before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that there is no point riding in a filthy bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges the nine letters of A DIRTY BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or foolishness is a thing in which there is no sense.

clue.text: A wild she-cat that can be trusted

definitions.note: a noun phrase in sense: one that can be trusted, a faithful companion

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the cat word are thrown about

explanation.surface: A feral female cat that, surprisingly, is reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges SHECAT into CHATES after A. Achates was the faithful friend of Aeneas in Virgil, so his name means a trusted companion.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aeneid the hero's loyal comrade is a byword for a faithful friend.

clue.text: Completely virtuous ? Take a step in that direction

definitions.text: Take a step in that direction

explanation.surface: Advice to someone striving after perfect goodness.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits into SIN LESS, which is the step towards being free of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without wrongdoing is perfect virtue, and committing fewer misdeeds is the way to get there.

clue.text: Contrive to conceal a fastener

indicators.note: to conceal says the answer is tucked away inside the words just before it

explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' points into contRIVE To.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal pin hammered to hold plates together is a fastening.

clue.text: Pepper's ghost and the like

parts.note: Pepper's ghost is a Victorian theatre trick using angled glass to make a phantom appear on stage

explanation.walkthrough: Pepper's ghost, named after John Henry Pepper, uses a sheet of glass to make a figure seem to float on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage tricks that deceive the eye with false appearances are visual deceptions of this sort.

clue.text: Poet as yet disguised

indicators.note: disguised means altered in appearance, so the letters are shown in another order

explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' rearranges AS YET.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Huge denizen of the Psalmist's deep

definitions.text: Huge denizen of the Psalmist's deep

parts.words: Huge denizen of the Psalmist's deep
parts.note: Psalm 104 speaks of a great sea creature made to play in the deep

explanation.walkthrough: Psalm 104 says of the sea 'there is that leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein'.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical sea monster of the Psalms is a vast creature living in the ocean depths.

clue.text: The criminal drops in at this house

indicators.note: drops means lets go of, so the word in is taken away from the word for the criminal

parts.note: a villain is a criminal

explanation.surface: A crook breaks into a particular house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' looks like visiting; 'drops' removes IN from VILLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or suburban residence.

clue.text: A hundred requests for drink containers

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
asks means requests

explanation.surface: A hundred people asking for drinks containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrels holding wine, beer or spirits are drink containers.

clue.text: Monographs as it might appear among trees

indicators.note: among puts the scrambled letters between the letters of the word trees
might appear suggests the letters could show up in another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scholarly texts appearing among the trees, as in a forest of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might appear' rearranges AS IT to ATIS, and 'among' sets ATIS inside TREES, TRE-ATIS-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Monographs are detailed written studies of one subject, which is what treatises are.

clue.text: Letters asking for, rent

parts.note: letters looks like written messages demanding money, but here means people who let property and collect rent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' are not correspondence but people who let, landlords who ask for rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords who grant leases let property and charge rent for it.

clue.text: It's still in the house, though moving underground

definitions.text: It's still in the house, though moving underground

parts.words: It's still in the house, though moving underground
parts.note: flights of steps in a home stay put, but the escalators of the London Underground are moving versions

explanation.walkthrough: An escalator on the London Underground is called a moving one; at home the same thing is still.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps between floors is fixed indoors, while an escalator is its moving form.

clue.text: Turned up in digs

parts.note: digs reads as lodgings, but it means excavations, where the earth beneath the topsoil is turned up by spades

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up in digs' sounds like arriving at lodgings; it is earth dug up from below the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The layer beneath the topsoil is brought to the surface when ground is dug deeply.

clue.text: Divine flowers, praise God !

parts.note: flowers here means things that flow, recalling the doxology 'Praise God from whom all good things flow'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' are things that flow: the hymn line is 'Praise God from whom all blessings flow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts of divine favour flow from God, as the doxology sings.

clue.text: They are known by their acts

definitions.text: They are known by their acts

parts.words: They are known by their acts
parts.note: acts reads as deeds, but means Acts of Parliament, the statutes legislators pass

explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts' are statutes, so legislators are known by the Acts they pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Legislators pass Acts, the laws by which their work is remembered.

clue.text: Equine establishment conned in force

indicators.note: in places the learned material inside the abbreviation for the force

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force
to con is to learn by heart, and multiplication tables are the classic thing conned at school

explanation.surface: A horse yard that has been swindled by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conned' looks like swindled, but its old sense is learnt by heart, as times tables are; TABLES goes inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Buildings where horses are kept and trained form an establishment for horses.

clue.text: Wild rose bed given Gilbert's Basingstoke treatment

indicators.note: wild means disordered, so the letters of the two garden words are scrambled

explanation.surface: An unruly flower bed brought to order by a magic word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges ROSE BED. In Gilbert and Sullivan's Ruddigore, Mad Margaret is calmed back to sanity by the word 'Basingstoke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert's madwoman is brought to her senses by the word, which is to be calmed and made rational.

clue.text: But its user needn't worry

parts.note: to fret is to worry, and this tool does the fretting, meaning cutting fretwork, so its user is spared it

explanation.walkthrough: Fret means worry, but also to cut ornamental fretwork; the saw frets so the user need not.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-bladed saw for cutting intricate patterns in wood frets the wood on its user's behalf.

clue.text: A kind of highway ?

parts.note: a road bridge carrying traffic over another road is a raised route, high in the air

explanation.walkthrough: A highway read literally is a way high up, which an elevated road crossing is.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevated road crossing above another is literally a high road.

clue.text: A pushing young Lancastrian

parts.note: pushing looks like ambitious, but a street trader pushes a cart; Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Lancashire, so a lad from it is a young Lancastrian

explanation.walkthrough: Barrow-in-Furness was a Lancashire town, so a boy from Barrow is a young Lancastrian; a street trader pushing a handcart is the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A street seller who wheels his goods on a handcart is a pushing youth.

clue.text: In Lancashire a vehicle goes up and up

definitions.note: stands for a place in Lancashire, a noun

indicators.note: goes up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A vehicle climbing a steep Lancashire hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns CAB into BAC; BACUP is a mill town in Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a small town in the Rossendale valley of Lancashire.

clue.text: Animal, one of a number in the pound

definitions.text: one of a number in the pound

explanation.surface: A beast held in the animal pound with others.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pound' looks like a dogs' home; it is the weight, which holds sixteen of these.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called this, and sixteen such weights make up a pound avoirdupois.

clue.text: Home of a bachelor queen ?

parts.note: She is the title of Rider Haggard's novel about the queen Ayesha, She-who-must-be-obeyed
BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: Where does an unmarried queen live?
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical Queen of Sheba came from this land; the queen of Haggard's novel 'She' gives SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient kingdom of the Bible was ruled by the queen who visited Solomon.

clue.text: She blushed for a king ?

parts.note: a woman's name followed by red, blushed, makes the name of an Anglo-Saxon king

explanation.walkthrough: Add RED (blushed) to this woman's name and you have Ethelred, the Anglo-Saxon king.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name which, with red added, gives the king Ethelred the Unready.

clue.text: What separates wickets (connected with a ball) ?

definitions.text: What separates wickets (connected with a ball) ?

parts.words: What separates wickets (connected with a ball) ?
parts.note: a cricket pitch is twenty-two yards between the two sets of stumps, a surveyor's measure of that length, and a ball is fettered to a prisoner by the same thing

explanation.walkthrough: The surveyor's chain is 22 yards, the length of a cricket pitch between the wickets; 'ball and chain' is the prisoner's fetter.
explanation.definitionFit: The old measure of twenty-two yards is exactly a pitch's length, and the shackle links a ball to an ankle.

clue.text: Novel footwear on a bird

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the first piece is followed by the second, as if the footwear stood on the bird

parts.note: a raven is a bird
a shoe is footwear

explanation.surface: An odd picture of a bird wearing a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for the footwear; it is the definition, Henry Kingsley's 1862 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Kingsley's Victorian book of that title is a novel.

clue.text: Charles was still a young one at forty-five

definitions.text: Charles was still a young one at forty-five

parts.words: Charles was still a young one at forty-five
parts.note: Charles Edward Stuart, Bonnie Prince Charlie, was called the Young claimant to the throne during the Jacobite rising of 1745

explanation.walkthrough: 'At forty-five' looks like his age; it is the Forty-Five, the 1745 Jacobite rising, when Charles was the Young Pretender.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant to a throne held by another is so called, and Charles Stuart was the Young one.

clue.text: Methods of disposing of beer on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the beer goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: on board a ship is between S and S, SS standing for steamship
ale is beer

explanation.surface: How to get rid of beer stocked on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword habit of putting something inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling things is a way of getting rid of them for money.
